title: Deep Learning Fundamentals: Gradient Descent vs Brute Force Optimization

cues.en: -: Hello and welcome back to the course on deep learning.
cues.zh: 講師：大家好，歡迎回深度學習。

cues.en: In today's tutorial, we're talking about gradient descent.
What we learned previously was that in order for a neural network to learn, what needs to happen is back propagation.
cues.zh: 先前學到，網路學習需要反向傳播。

cues.en: And that is when the error, the difference or the sum of square differences between Y hat and Y is back propagated through the neural network
cues.zh: 將誤差，也就是 ŷ 和 y 的差異或平方差總和，往網路反傳，

cues.en: and the weights are adjusted accordingly.
So we saw that and today we're going to learn exactly how these weights are adjusted.
So let's have a look.
This is our very simple version of a neural network a perceptron or a single layer feed forward neural network.
cues.zh: 這是簡單網路，感知器、單層前饋網路。

cues.en: And what we can see here is this whole process in action where we've got some input value, then we've got a weight,
cues.zh: 這裡看到流程，輸入值、權重，

cues.en: then a activation function is applied.
We have, we get y hat and then we compare it to the actual value, we calculate the cost function.
cues.zh: 得到 ŷ，與真實比較，算成本。

cues.en: So how can we minimize the cost function?
What can we do about it?
Well, one approach to do it is a brute force approach where we just take all lots of different possible weights and look at them and see which one works best.
cues.zh: 一個暴力法，取很多不同權重，看看哪個最好。

cues.en: And what we do is, for instance, we'd try out for, let's say for example, a thousand weights and we'd try them out.
We'd get something like this for the cost function.
And this is a chart of on the Y axis you have cost function or vertical axis.
On the horizontal axis you have Y hat.
And because you can see the formula is Y hat minus Y squared, this is what the cost function would look something like that.
cues.zh: 公式是 ŷ 減 y 再平方，所以曲線如此。

cues.en: And basically you'd find the best one is over here.
So very simple, very intuitive approach.
Why not do this brute force method?
Why not just try out a thousand different cost thousand different parameters or inputs for weights and see which one works the best?
cues.zh: 試一千個不同權重參數，找最好？

cues.en: You'll find the best one that way.
Well, if you have just one way to optimize, this might work.
cues.zh: 只最佳化一個權重，可能可行。

cues.en: But as you increase the number of weights increase the number of synapses in your network you have to face the curse of dimensionality.
cues.zh: 但權重、突觸數增加，就面對維度詛咒。

cues.en: And so what is the curse of dimensionality?
The best way to describe this or explain it is to just look at a practical example.
So remember this example we had when we were talking about how neural networks actually work, where we were building or running a neural network
cues.zh: 記得談網路如何運作時的

cues.en: for a for a property valuation.
So this is what it looked like when it was trained up already.
Well, when it's not trained before, it's trained before we know which, what are the weights, the actual neural network looks like this, right?
cues.zh: 訓練前、不知道權重時，實際這樣。

cues.en: Because we have all these different possible synapses and we still have to train up the weights.
cues.zh: 有各種可能突觸，還得訓練權重。

cues.en: And here we have a total of 25 weights.
So four times five at the start, plus five more from the hidden layer to the output layer, 25 weights total.
cues.zh: 起始 4 乘 5，再隱藏到輸出 5，合計 25。

cues.en: And let's see how we could possibly brute force 25 weight.
It's a very simple neural network right here.
Very simple, just one hidden layer.
And how could we brute force our way through a neural network of this size?
Well, let's do some simple mathematical calculations.
We have 25 weights.

So that means if we have a thousand combinations that we're gonna test out for every weight, the total number of combinations is a thousand to the power of 25 or a thousand or 10 to the power of 75 different combinations.
cues.zh: 每個試一千，總組合一千的 25 次方，也就是 10 的 75 次方。

cues.en: Now, let's see how Sunway TaihuLight, the world's fastest super computer as of June, 2016.
cues.zh: 看看截至 2016 年六月，全球最快的神威太湖之光，

cues.en: What, how would it approach this problem?
Right, so Sunway TaihuLight looks like this is a whole huge building pretty much for this one super computer.
cues.zh: 長這樣，幾乎整棟大建築放一台超級電腦。

cues.en: And it got the Guinness World Record for being the fastest supercomputer.
cues.zh: 拿到最快超級電腦金氏紀錄。

cues.en: Right now it is the fastest super computer in the world and Sunway TaihuLight can operate at a speed of 93 petaflops.
cues.zh: 當時全球最快，速度 93 petaflops。

cues.en: Flop stands for floating operation per second.
So it can do 93 to the power times 10 to the power of 15 floating operations per second.
cues.zh: 每秒 93 乘 10 的 15 次方次浮點運算。

cues.en: That's how quick it is.
In comparison, average computers right now they do like just over several gigaflops and so on.
cues.zh: 相較普通電腦大約幾 gigaflops。

cues.en: So it kind of those ranges way less than Sunway TaihuLight.
So Sunway TaihuLight is in the forefront of technology and let's say hypothetically that it can do one test
cues.zh: 最前沿技術，假設一次測試，

cues.en: one combination for our neural network in one flop, basically in one floating operation.
cues.zh: 也就是網路一組組合，只需一次浮點運算。

cues.en: That is not possible.
That is not practical because you need multiple floating operations to test out a single weight in your neural network.
cues.zh: 不實際，測一個權重就要多次運算。

cues.en: But even let's give it a head start.
Let's say that it can do that.
In a ideal world, it can do that in one floating operation.
cues.zh: 理想世界，一次浮點就可。

cues.en: It can do one test per one floating operation.
That means it will still require 10 to the power of 75 divided by 93 times 10 to power of 15 seconds
cues.zh: 仍需 10 的 75 次方，除以 93 乘 10 的 15 次方秒，

cues.en: to come to run all of those tests to brute force through that network.
cues.zh: 才能跑完、暴力搜完整網路。

cues.en: So that means one or approximately 10 to the power of 58 seconds, and that is the same as 10 to the power of 50 years.
cues.zh: 約 10 的 58 次方秒，相當於 10 的 50 次方年。

cues.en: That is a huge number that is longer than the universe has existed.
cues.zh: 巨大，比宇宙存在時間更久。

cues.en: And that is definitely not going to, simply this number is so huge, it's just definitely not going to work for us at all in our optimization.
cues.zh: 太大，最佳化完全行不通。

cues.en: So there we go.
This is a no-no, even on the world's fastest super computer Sunway TaihuLight.
cues.zh: 連全球最快神威都不行。

cues.en: So we have to come up with a different approach.
How we going to find the optimal weight?
By the way, this, our neural network was very simple.
What about if the neural networks looks like something like this, right?
Or even greater than that, then yeah it's just not going to happen at all, ever.
So the method we're going to be looking at is called gradient descent.
cues.zh: 要看的方法叫梯度下降。

cues.en: And you may have heard of it already.
If not, we will find out what it is right now.
So there's our cost function and now we're going to see how we can faster come
cues.zh: 成本函數在這，看看怎更快

cues.en: of a faster way to find the best option.
So let's say we start somewhere.
You gotta start somewhere.
So we start over there and from that point in the top left what we're going to do is we're going to look
at the angle of our cost function at that point.
So we're just going to basically, that's why it's called gradient, because you have to differentiate.
cues.zh: 因此叫梯度，因為要微分。

cues.en: We're not going to look at the mathematical equations.
We will provide some tips on additional reading at the end of the next lecture.
cues.zh: 下一堂末提供延伸閱讀建議。

cues.en: But basically you just need to differentiate, find out what the slope is in that specific point and find out if the slope is positive or negative.
cues.zh: 基本上微分，找該點斜率、判斷正負。

cues.en: If the, if the slope is negative like in this case means that it, you're going downhill.
So to the right is downhill to the left is uphill.
And from there it means you need to go, right.
Basically you need to go downhill.
And that's what we're going to do.
Room takes a step, right?
The ball rolls down.
Again, same thing.
You calculate the slope.
This time the slope is positive, meaning right is uphill left is downhill and you need to go left and you roll the ball down.
cues.zh: 這次正，右上坡、左下坡，所以往左、球往下滾。

cues.en: And again you calculate the slope and you roll the ball right.
There we go.
So that's how you find in simple terms that's how you find the best weights the best situation that minimizes your cost function.
cues.zh: 簡單說，這樣找最小化成本的最佳權重、最佳狀況。

cues.en: Of course, it's not going to be like a ball rolling it's going to be a very zigzaggy type of approach but it's easier to remember or kind of, it's more fun to look at it as a ball rolling.
cues.zh: 當然不真像滾球，是鋸齒狀，但滾球好記、有趣。

cues.en: But in reality, yes, you just it is going to be like a step by step approach.
So it's gonna be a zigzaggy type of method.
Yeah, and also there's lots of other elements to it.
There's things like, for instance, why, like why does it go down?
Why does it not like go away over the line?
So it could have jumped out of this, gone upwards instead of downwards and things like that.
cues.zh: 可能跳出去，往上而非下等等。

cues.en: So there are parameters that you can tweak, and again we will mention where you can find out more on that.
cues.zh: 有可調參數，也會提供深入資訊來源。

cues.en: And plus we'll have this in the practical application.
But in the simplest intuitive approach this is what is happening.
We are getting to the bottom by just understanding which way we need to go.
Instead of brute forcing through thousands and thousands and millions and billions and quadrillions of combinations we can just simply every time have a look
cues.zh: 不用暴力搜數千、百萬、十億、兆兆組合，只要每次看

cues.en: at where is, where, which way is it sloping?
So right like you are, you imagine you're standing on a hill, which way does it feel that it's going downwards?
cues.zh: 想像站山坡，哪邊感覺下坡？

cues.en: And whichever way it is going downwards you just keep walking that where you like.
You take 50 steps that way and then you assess again, okay which way is it going downwards?
cues.zh: 走五十步，再評估下坡方向。

cues.en: This way, okay, now take 50 steps or less, take 40 steps that way.
cues.zh: 這裡？好，走五十，或少點四十步。

cues.en: So it gets less and less and less as you get closer.
So here's an example of gradient descent applied in a two dimensional space.
cues.zh: 這是二維空間梯度下降。

cues.en: So that was a one dimensional example.
Here we have a two dimensional space for the gradient descent.
As you can see, it's getting closer to the minimum and it's also called gradient descent because you're descending into the minimum of the cost function.
cues.zh: 越近最小值，叫下降因為降到成本最小值。

cues.en: And finally here's the gradient descent applied in three dimensions.
This is what it looks like if you project it onto two dimensions, you can see it's zigzagging its way into the minimum.
cues.zh: 投影二維，就看到鋸齒走向最小值。

cues.en: So there we go.
That was gradient descent.
In next tutorial we'll talk about stochastic gradient descent is will be a continuation of this tutorial and I look forward to seeing you there.
cues.zh: 下一堂隨機梯度下降，延續這堂，期待再見。

cues.en: Until next time, enjoy deep learning.
cues.zh: 在那之前，祝你享受深度學習的樂趣。
